chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:
There is no problem with smelling the idhkhir, the qaysum, the khuzama, the shi'ah, and their like, while you are in the state of ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.إِذْخِرٌ: A type of aromatic plant (Chenopodium ambrosioides) used as perfume
key_terms.خُزَامَى: A type of aromatic plant (Sarcocornia) used as perfume
key_terms.شِّيحٌ: Wormwood (Artemisia), an aromatic plant used as perfume
key_terms.قَيْصُومٌ: A type of aromatic plant (Achilles) used as perfume
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What perfumes are permissible to smell while in the state of Ihram according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the prohibition of 'thiob' (perfume) in ihram specifically targets the scent of plants, not their natural aroma, allowing pilgrims to smell aromatic herbs like idhkhir and qaysum without breaking their state. This ruling distinguishes between the general prohibition of wearing or consuming scented items and the permissibility of utilizing their natural fragrance for comfort or medicinal purposes during the sacred rites.
